gone.ask_friend: Have you seen Stitches lately? Could you talk to him for me?
gone.goodbye_note: I won't bother you anymore. Thank you for all the food. You're a really good cook. I hope your restaurant is always busy. — S.

letter.reply: I got your letter. I read it a lot of times. ...I'll come by. Just once.

choices.text: Dear Stitches, I'm so sorry for how I treated you.
Stitches, I owe you an apology.
Hey, Stitches! Long time no see.
You never deserved any of it. You were always kind to me.
I was rude to you, and that was wrong.
I was a bit of a grump, huh?
The corner table is yours whenever you want it. I'd really like to see you.
Come by if you want.
The pancakes miss you!

lines.text: Is the corner one free? ...Only if it's okay.
I can sit anywhere. Well. The corner, if I could. Sorry.
The corner, please. It's kind of my table now. Is that weird?
My corner! You kept it free. ...You didn't keep it free. But it feels like you did.
Can I try a middle table today? ...Okay. Okay! I'm doing it.
The corner, please. Not to hide! You can see everybody from there. I like watching everyone be happy here.
The corner's fine.

after.narration: He heads off before you can lead him.

lines.text: Um... could I have a hot chocolate? If it's not too much trouble.
Just water is fine. ...Actually, could I have a hot chocolate? Sorry. Hot chocolate.
Hot chocolate, please. With a marshmallow, if you have one. I won't be upset if you don't.
I'll try a [drink] today. Being brave.
Hot chocolate, please, [name]. The marshmallow is my favorite part. I save it for last.
Do you have a favorite drink? ...I want to try it.
Hot chocolate. Two marshmallows. I'm a two-marshmallow bear now.
Surprise me with a drink, too! I like surprises now.
Water, please. I don't need anything special.
Water.
You brought a marshmallow. ...Thank you. Really.
It's perfect. You always make it perfect, [name].
Thank you. It's really nice.
Thank you.
Oh... um. Hi. I'm Stitches. Is it okay if I sit here? In the corner? I won't be in the way.
Oh... you're open. I came by a few times. It was closed. I thought maybe... never mind. I'm glad you're okay.
Last time was... it was fine! Really. I ate all of it.
I kept thinking about my last meal here. Is that weird? Sorry.
Sorry. Hi. I'm back. If that's okay.
Um... is the corner table free? It's fine if it's not.
Hello... I hope it's not too busy. I can come back later if it is.
[name]! You're back. I walked past every day, just in case.
I told my reflection about your cooking. It was the only one listening. Ha. That was a joke.
Hi, [name]. ...I practiced saying your name on the way here. Is that weird? Don't answer that.
I'm back! I mean. Hi. A normal amount of excited.
You're back! I missed this place. I missed... you know. Talking to you.
Last time was a little crispy. I'm only telling you because you said I could be honest with you.
[name]! Guess what. I finished a new patch. Look, it has little stars on it.
I saved the corner table. ...Okay, nobody else ever takes it. But I saved it anyway.
There you are! I was about to sew a 'missing chef' poster.
[name]! I'm here! Your favorite customer! ...Is that too much? No. I'm owning it.
I sat at a middle table today. In the middle. Where people can see me. Are you proud of me? You can say yes.
I keep thinking about when you said "[last_rude_line]". ...I'm sure you were just busy.
Hi... um. Did I do something wrong last time? You can tell me. I'll fix it.
Thank you. Sorry for the trouble. I wiped the table already.
I'll... maybe come back? If that's okay.
See you soon, [name]. I still wiped the table. Old habits.
Can I leave the table for you this time? ...I trust you not to mind.
Bye, [name]! Same time tomorrow? I'm not asking. I'm telling you.
Thank you. Sorry.
Thank you.
Oh... it's beautiful. You made this? For me? Thank you. Really.
Thank you so much. It smells really nice.
It's... it's perfect. Thank you.
Thank you, [name]. It looks so good. I'm going to eat it slowly so it lasts.
You remembered I like it warm. ...Or you didn't, and I'm just lucky. Either way.
You burnt the edge a little. I'm still eating all of it. I'm just letting you know I noticed.
[name], this looks amazing. You always make me feel like I'm worth the effort.
Thank you. Sorry.
Oh! Hi. Is something wrong? Am I eating too slow?
It's quiet in here today. I like quiet. ...I'm used to it.
Sorry if I'm staring at the kitchen. It's nice watching someone make something with care.
Do you ever feel like you're too much? Or not enough? ...Sorry. That's a big question for lunch.
I could fix that loose button on your apron. If you want. I'm good at fixing things. Just not myself. ...That was a joke! Mostly.
I used to think my patches made me broken. Now I think they just make me... me.
I said hi to someone at the park today. First. I went first. My heart was pounding.
Do you need anything mended? I mean it. You've fixed a lot for me. Let me fix something for you.
Did you need something? I'm almost done. I'll go soon.
Um... I'll just have whatever's easiest for you. I don't want to make extra work.

choices.text: You're never extra work. Order what you really want.
choices.reply: ...Really? Okay. Then the [dish]. Thank you. Thank you.

choices.text: Easiest for me is nothing. Want a bowl of air?
choices.reply: Ha... that was funny. I think.

choices.text: Just tell me what you want.
choices.reply: S-sorry. The [dish]. Sorry.

choices.text: Then hurry up and pick. People are waiting.
choices.reply: ...Right. Sorry. The [dish].

lines.text: Sorry, I'm slow to decide. Everything sounds nice. That's a good problem, I guess.

choices.text: Take all the time you need. I'll wait.
choices.reply: ...Nobody ever says that to me.

choices.text: Close your eyes and point at the menu.
choices.reply: Okay... oh! That's a good one, actually.

choices.text: I'll come back in a minute.
choices.reply: Okay. Sorry.

choices.text: Seriously? It's not that hard.
choices.reply: ...I know. I'm sorry.

lines.text: Sorry, my paw's stitching came loose again. Please don't mind it.

choices.text: Your stitching is really neat. Did you do it yourself?
choices.reply: ...You noticed? I did. Thank you.

choices.text: It matches the tablecloth. Very stylish.
choices.reply: Oh... does it? I didn't plan that.

choices.text: No problem. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: Just don't get stuffing in the food.
choices.reply: ...I'll be careful.

lines.text: I tried to guess what I'd order on the way here. I changed my mind three times.

choices.text: Whatever you pick will be the right choice.
choices.reply: ...You always say nice things. I'm not used to it yet.

choices.text: Let me guess for you. I'm amazing at guessing.
choices.reply: You'll just pick what you're best at making! ...That was a joke. Was it okay?

choices.text: What did you land on?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: Can you not ramble? I'm busy.
choices.reply: Oh... right. Sorry.

lines.text: How's your day been? You always ask about mine. It's your turn.

choices.text: Better now that you're here.
choices.reply: You can't just say things like that. Now I'll be smiling all day.

choices.text: A customer asked about my day. Very suspicious.
choices.reply: Okay, okay! I'll order! The [dish].

choices.text: Busy, but good.
choices.reply: I'm glad. Don't work too hard, okay?

choices.text: Why do you even care?
choices.reply: ...Because I do. Sorry. I'll just order.

lines.text: I'm going to order something I've never tried. Old me would never. New me is brave. Mostly.

choices.text: I'm really proud of you, you know.
choices.reply: ...Don't make me cry before I've even eaten.

choices.text: New you better tip less than old you.
choices.reply: Never! Old me and new me agree on tipping.

choices.text: Go for it. I'll make it good.
choices.reply: I know you will.

choices.text: Nobody cares, just order.
choices.reply: ...Oh. Okay.

lines.text: I'll be quick. I won't bother you.
The [dish]. Please.
Can I tell you something? This is the only place where nobody stares at my patches.

choices.text: They're part of you. I like them.
choices.reply: ...Okay.

choices.text: Everyone's too busy staring at my cooking.
choices.reply: Ha! That's true. It's very stare-able.

choices.text: Glad you feel comfortable here.
choices.reply: I really do.

choices.text: Probably because you hide in the corner.
choices.reply: ...Yeah. Probably.

lines.text: When I was little, my ear got torn off in a fight I didn't start. I sewed it back on myself. It came out crooked. It's still crooked.

choices.text: You fixed it yourself. That's brave.
choices.reply: Nobody ever called it brave. They called it ugly.

choices.text: Crooked ears are in this season.
choices.reply: Then I'm very fashionable.

choices.text: Yeah, I can tell.

lines.text: Um, [name]? What would you recommend? You'd know better than me.

favorite.text: This is my favorite. How did you know? ...Did you remember?

disliked.text: Oh! It's good. I'm going to eat all of it.

other.text: I'll trust you. You haven't been wrong yet.

lines.text: Surprise me. I trust you completely.

favorite.text: You KNOW me. This is the best day.

disliked.text: Okay. I need to confess something. I've never liked this one. I just never wanted to hurt your feelings.

other.text: New! I like new things now. That's new too.

lines.text: Can I ask your name? You know mine. It feels rude that I don't know yours.

choices.text: (Tell him your name.)
choices.reply: [name]. That's a nice name. I'll remember it. I promise.

lines.text: [restaurant]... I like that name. It sounds like a place where people are allowed to stay a while.
Is it okay if I say [restaurant] is my favorite place? ...It is. Sorry. It just is.
Hi! ...Walking into [restaurant] feels a little like coming home. Is that weird? Don't answer that.
The tortoise lady, Mabel, said hello to me today. She asked if I made my patches. She said they're lovely.
...Hello. It's Stitches. For delivery. Sorry.
Hi. It's me. I'd like to order. From home. If that's okay.
Thank you for the note. I read it a few times. ...The [dish], please.
The [dish]. For the corner table person. No need to rush. Sorry.
That's all. ...Bye.

choices.text: (Tuck a note in his bag: "I'm sorry. Your corner table misses you.")
(Just send the food.)
(Tuck a note in his bag: "Stop calling here.")

lines.text: Hi, [name]! It's Stitches. I'm not ordering anything. I just... wanted to call someone. And you were the first one I thought of. Okay. Bye!
Hi. ...I almost didn't come in. That's twice now, at this restaurant.

choices.text: I'm so sorry. You didn't deserve any of it.
choices.reply: ...I kept thinking it was my fault. That I was too much.

choices.text: I was cruel to you. There's no excuse.
choices.reply: Thank you for not making one.

choices.text: I want to start over, if you'll let me.
choices.reply: Starting over is okay. I'm good at fixing things.

lines.text: I forgive you. I think I already did, a little, before I even walked in. ...Can I have the corner table? Just for now.
Mabel told me about the bell. She said it's in good hands. She looked really happy, [name].
Oh! You came. You actually— um. Hi. Sorry. I wasn't sure you'd... hi.
Hi! Sorry, I was sewing. I've got thread on me. Everywhere. Sorry.
Oh, hi! I was awake. I'm always awake around now. Is that weird? It's quiet, so I sew.
The porch light's new. I put it in so you could find the door. ...In case. Not that I was expecting you. I was a bit.
I counted the steps up to my door once. One. I don't know why I told you that.
Is it okay if we just sit here a bit? Not talking? ...Okay. Good. This is nice.
I can see your restaurant from my window. When the lights are on, it feels less dark over here.
Okay. Bye. Thank you for coming. Really. Bye.
Goodnight! Um. Come back? If you want? You don't have to. But you can.
Come in! Um, if you want. It's small. Mind the bed, it's sort of in the way.
It's Friday! Fridays are the best day for visitors. I decided that just now. Come in!
Sit anywhere! Oh, not there, there's pins. Sorry. Anywhere else!
I tidied. You can't tell. I tidied a lot, though.
I made the rug. Well, I mended it. It came with a hole. Everything comes with a hole. That's okay.
I used to hide the patches. Big jackets in summer. Now I sort of like them. Each one's a day I got through.
Sometimes I talk to the couch cushions. They're good listeners. You're better, though.
Mabel came by once. She said the house was "charming." I think that was good? She said it the way she says "soup."
Thank you for coming inside. Nobody's really come inside before.
Bye! Be careful going home. Look both ways. Twice. Okay, bye!
[name]! Come in, come in! I was hoping it was you. I made extra pancakes. In case.
Oh good, you're here! I couldn't sleep, and now I don't have to try.
Welcome home! I mean, welcome to my home. Same thing, kind of. Sit!
I saved you the comfy end of the couch. The other end has a spring. I'm fixing it.
I'm making you all aprons. With pockets. Lots of pockets. You can never have enough pockets.
I used to think I had to be fixed before anyone would like me. Turns out you just liked me. Patches and everything.
I go to the restaurant even when I'm not hungry now. Just to say hi. Is that okay? ...I know it's okay. I just like hearing it.
Cheddar showed me a card trick. I figured it out. I didn't tell him. Don't tell him.
Bye! Come back soon! Tomorrow's soon. Tomorrow's good.
Goodnight, [name]. Thank you for being my friend. I don't say it enough. Okay, I say it a lot. I mean it every time.
That's my sewing kit. My grandma gave it to me. The blue thread's the same blue as my very first patch.
I can fix anything with that. Well. Most things. Things, anyway. People are harder.
That's Button. He's got even more patches than me. I practised on him first. He was very brave.
Button was the first friend I ever fixed. You're the first friends who fixed me. ...Sorry. That was a lot.
(Through the door, very quietly:) Oh! Um. It's not— it's not a good time. Sorry. I'm sorry.
(The lights go off inside. Then, after a moment:) ...Sorry. Not tonight. Sorry.
(Through the door:) I don't... I don't really feel like company tonight. Sorry.
(A shuffle behind the door.) Maybe another time? I'm just a bit mixed up. Sorry.
(Through the door, small:) Please, not tonight.
(A long pause. Then:) ...Not tonight. Goodnight.
(Through the door:) Oh, hi again! I'm in my pyjamas now. Tomorrow? Tomorrow!
(The curtain moves. A patched paw waves.) Tomorrow! I'll make something!
(Through the door:) Again? You're so nice. But I'm so sleepy. Tomorrow?
For me? Is it— it is! [gift]! Oh, thank you. Thank you thank you. Sorry. Thank you.
[gift]... you knew. How did you know? ...Thank you, [name]. Really.
Oh, [gift]! I love— I like— I really like it. Thank you!
You brought me [gift]? Nobody brings me things. Thank you.
[gift]! Thank you. I'll keep it somewhere safe. Somewhere special.
Oh! Um. [gift]. Thank you! I'm not sure what it's for, but I'll treasure it.
